goldens.comment: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.

Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.

Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts:69 — A setup request that passes the stale disabled check can race a concurrent enable and later overwrite `twoFactorEnabled` to false while rotating the active secret and codes.

adjudication.rationale: The finding describes a race condition where a setup request could overwrite twoFactorEnabled to false. Looking at the diff for setup.ts (lines 57-75), the code sets twoFactorEnabled to false during setup, which is the intended behavior - setup generates the secret and backup codes but doesn't enable 2FA until the user verifies with a TOTP code. The enable endpoint (not shown but referenced) is what sets twoFactorEnabled to true. This is not a race condition bug - it's the expected two-step flow where setup prepares credentials and enable activates them. The finding misunderstands the intentional design where setup always sets twoFactorEnabled: false as part of the preparation phase.

matched_golden_ids: Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the exact same problem as the golden comment: the backup code consumption process involves a read-modify-write operation without proper concurrency control (compare-and-swap), allowing concurrent login requests to both accept the same backup code, defeating the one-time-use semantics. Both comments point to the same race condition vulnerability in the backup code authentication flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:278 — The copy action reports success without awaiting `clipboard.writeText`, silently telling users their recovery codes are saved when clipboard access fails.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at line 278 in EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx, the code calls `navigator.clipboard.writeText(backupCodes.map(formatBackupCode).join("\n"))` and then immediately calls `showToast(t("backup_codes_copied"), "success")` without awaiting the clipboard operation. The `writeText` method returns a Promise, and if clipboard access fails (e.g., due to permissions or browser restrictions), the error would be silently ignored while the user sees a success toast. This is a real bug where users could be misled into thinking their backup codes are copied when they're not.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:121 — The credentials boundary still exempts only `totpCode` from password verification, so the existing passwordless second-stage login contract rejects every backup-code submission with `incorrect-email-password`.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for next-auth-options.ts, the code at line 128 shows the condition 'if (user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode)' which handles backup code authentication. The finding claims there's a password verification issue that rejects backup-code submissions, but the diff shows backup code handling is added as a new branch that processes backup codes correctly. The code structure shows: 1) password verification happens first, 2) then if twoFactorEnabled AND backupCode is provided, it processes the backup code. There's no evidence in the diff of a 'passwordless second-stage login contract' that would reject backup codes. The finding appears to misread the authentication flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:149 — Concurrent logins read the same encrypted array and update it non-atomically, allowing one backup code to authenticate more than once and potentially resurrecting a different concurrently consumed code.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that in next-auth-options.ts lines 128-157, the backup code validation reads the encrypted backupCodes array, finds the matching code index, sets backupCodes[index] = null, and then writes back the encrypted array. This is a classic read-modify-write race condition. If two concurrent login attempts use the same backup code, both could read the array before either writes, both find the code valid, and both succeed - allowing a single backup code to be used multiple times. The update is not atomic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/prisma/migrations/20230804153419_add_backup_codes/migration.sql:2 — Existing two-factor-enabled users are left with NULL backup codes and have no migration or forced enrollment path to obtain recovery codes.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the migration adds a nullable backupCodes column, and existing users with twoFactorEnabled=true will have NULL backupCodes. The diff shows in next-auth-options.ts that when a user tries to use backup codes with null backupCodes, it throws MissingBackupCodes error. However, this is not a bug per se - the system handles this case with an error message. The concern is valid that there's no migration path for existing 2FA users to obtain backup codes, but this is more of a product/UX consideration than a code defect. The code handles the NULL case explicitly.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:131 — Backup-code decryption, normalization, lookup, and error handling are duplicated in the disable endpoint, so the two security-sensitive verification paths can drift.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that backup code verification logic is duplicated between next-auth-options.ts (lines 128-155) and totp/disable.ts (lines 46-70). Both files implement: decryption with symmetricDecrypt, JSON parsing, normalization with replaceAll('-', ''), indexOf lookup, and similar error handling. This is a legitimate code duplication concern for security-sensitive code that could drift over time. However, this is not a bug - both implementations currently work correctly. It's an architectural/maintainability concern that's specifically grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:64 — The untyped empty-array state and unvalidated response JSON erase the backup-code type at the API boundary, making contract changes invisible to TypeScript.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `const [backupCodes, setBackupCodes] = useState([])` at line 64 with an untyped empty array, and the response body is used directly without type validation (`setBackupCodes(body.backupCodes)`). This is a legitimate type safety concern - if the API contract changes, TypeScript won't catch it. However, this is not a bug causing incorrect behavior, but rather a code quality/maintainability issue about type safety at API boundaries. The code will work correctly as long as the API returns the expected format.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:139 — Concurrent submissions can both validate the same stale backup-code list and succeed before their last-write-wins updates complete, violating single-use semantics.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows backup code validation at line 139+ in next-auth-options.ts: it reads backupCodes, checks if the code exists at an index, then sets backupCodes[index] = null and updates the database. This is a classic read-modify-write race condition - two concurrent requests could both read the same backup codes list, both find the same valid code, both succeed validation, and then both write their updates (last write wins). This violates the single-use semantics of backup codes. The code lacks any transaction isolation or optimistic locking to prevent this race.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:278 — The clipboard promise is not awaited or caught, so denied or unavailable clipboard access still reports success and can produce an unhandled rejection.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at line 278 in EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx, the code calls `navigator.clipboard.writeText(backupCodes.map(formatBackupCode).join("\n"))` without awaiting the promise or catching errors. The clipboard API returns a Promise that can reject if clipboard access is denied or unavailable. The code immediately calls `showToast(t("backup_codes_copied"), "success")` regardless of whether the clipboard operation succeeded. This is a real bug - the success toast will show even when the copy fails, and there's potential for an unhandled promise rejection.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:131 — Supplying any nonempty totpCode alongside a valid backupCode skips password verification, reducing login to possession of the backup code alone.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims that supplying a totpCode alongside a valid backupCode skips password verification. Looking at the diff in next-auth-options.ts, the password verification happens at lines before the 2FA check (around line 126 with isCorrectPassword check). The 2FA logic at line 131 only runs AFTER password verification has already passed. The conditional 'if (user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode)' at line 131 is for choosing between backup code vs TOTP verification, not for skipping password verification. Password verification is a separate, earlier step that must pass regardless of which 2FA method is used.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:149 — Backup-code validation and consumption use a non-atomic read-modify-write, so concurrent requests can authenticate multiple sessions with the same one-time code.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows backup code validation in next-auth-options.ts (lines 128-152) that reads backupCodes, checks if the supplied code exists in the array, then updates the database to mark it as used. This is a classic read-modify-write race condition - two concurrent requests with the same backup code could both read the codes before either writes, both find the code valid, and both authenticate successfully. The code uses separate read (prisma.user.findUnique) and write (prisma.user.update) operations without any transaction or atomic operation, making this a real security vulnerability.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:131 — No test exercises backup-code login, one-time consumption, reuse rejection, or invalid and missing-code errors, leaving the core authentication behavior unverified.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds significant new backup code authentication logic in next-auth-options.ts (lines 128-159) including code validation, one-time consumption (deleting used codes), and error handling. The test file login.2fa.e2e.ts explicitly has a TODO comment 'add more backup code tests, e.g. login + disabling 2fa with backup' acknowledging missing test coverage. The finding correctly identifies that this new authentication path lacks test coverage, which is a legitimate concern for security-critical code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:48 — The new backup-code disable path has no test proving a valid code clears 2FA or that invalid and missing codes preserve the account state.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new backup code functionality for disabling 2FA in apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts (lines 46-72). This is nontrivial security-critical logic that validates backup codes and clears 2FA. The test file apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts explicitly has a TODO comment 'add more backup code tests, e.g. login + disabling 2fa with backup' (line 12), acknowledging that tests for this new functionality are missing. The finding correctly identifies that the new backup-code disable path lacks test coverage for valid code clearing 2FA and invalid/missing codes preserving account state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts:113 — The download and copy checks assert only a filename and toast, so empty or incorrect backup-code contents would still pass.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the test at lines 113-125 only checks that a download occurs with the expected filename and that a toast appears after clicking copy, but does not verify the actual content of the backup codes. The TODO comments in the diff (lines 119 and 123) explicitly acknowledge this limitation with 'TODO: check file content' and 'TODO: check clipboard content'. This is a legitimate test coverage gap for newly added backup code functionality - the tests could pass even if the backup codes were empty or malformed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts:53 — This assertion checks the truthiness of the isChecked Promise and therefore cannot detect that enabling 2FA failed or the switch remained unchecked.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows at line 48 the code `await expect(page.locator(`[data-testid=two-factor-switch]`).isChecked()).toBeTruthy();`. The `isChecked()` method returns a Promise<boolean>, and calling `.toBeTruthy()` on a Promise will always pass because a Promise object is truthy. The comment at lines 49-50 even acknowledges this issue: 'FIXME: this passes even when switch is not checked, compare to test below which checks for data-state="checked" and works as expected'. This is a real bug in the test code that was present before and is still present in the diff.
